articleTitle: Pulsed power accelerator technology based on solid-state semiconductor opening switches (SOS)
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In 1991 we discovered a semiconductor opening switch (SOS) effect that occurs at a current density of up to 60 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The discovery of the effect provided a basis for the development of an opening switch with a gigawatt level of pulsed power, with an interrupted current of scores of kilo amperes, with a voltage of up to 0.5 MV, and with a current interruption time of 10 to 50 ns. Subsequent to those experiments, we developed a new circuitry ideology of constructing repetitive megavolt generators and accelerators with an all-solid-state switching system. In this approach, the SOS performs the function of a terminal power amplifier, by transforming the microsecond pumping pulse into a nanosecond output pulse. Significantly, the thyristor transformer delivers power to the SOS via an intermediate magnetic compressor. We present results of theoretical and experimental investigations of the SOS effect and describe the circuits and design of accelerators developed on the basis of it.

articleTitle: Results of the reacceleration experiment: Experimental study of the relativistic klystron two-beam accelerator concept
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We recently demonstrated the reacceleration of a bunched beam through an induction accelerator cell in support of the two-beam accelerator concept. We present the results of this experiment including amplitude and phase measurements of the extracted microwave power at 11.424 GHz. We also describe progress in achieving a two-beam accelerator microwave source design that is efficient and cost effective for linear collider applications.

articleTitle: New results of the full scale ribbon beam experiments on U-2 device
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The paper presents the experimental results on generating and transforming the ribbon (3.5×130cm) beam with the electron energy 1 MeV, beam current up to 7kA and pulse duration 8 µs. 70% efficiency of the energy transfer from a capacitor storage to 0.4MJ ribbon beam has been obtained. The similar efficiency has been also achieved for the transformation of the ribbon beam to a compressed circular one at the optimal conditions. Measurements have shown an angular spread of the compressed beam is less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>.

articleTitle: ACE 4 inductive energy storage power conditioning performance
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A slow plasma flashboard source was designed and tested on ACE 4. While the optimized slow plasma flashboard source was capable of providing a intergap density profile which exhibited thinning during the conduction phase based on the snowplow model, it did not sufficiently localize the POS opening in the compact radial ACE 4 geometry to allow coupling to a load.

articleTitle: The nonlinear autosynchronization in beam-plasma interaction
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The problem of overcoming the saturation of beam-plasma interaction caused by particles trapping is considered. Some results of efficiency enhancement for microwave generation and particle acceleration are discussed, On a simple model of dissipative beam-plasma instability the interaction increasing is shown due to the self consistent nonlinear synchronization between beam and phase velocities.

articleTitle: Making PARMILA easy to use - really easy to use!
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A graphical user interface (GUI), which provides for easy problem set up and dam input, has been integrated with the PARMILA program. PARMILA is one of the most commonly used simulation programs for the design and analysis of high power radio frequency ion accelerators. Despite the widespread use of. PARMILA, the initial set up of a design problem can be tedious and time consuming, even for experienced users. We have developed a new approach to using PARMILA by integrating it with the Shell for Particle Accelerator Related Codes (SPARC), a unique GUI designed specifically to support particle beam simulation and analysis programs. Using SPARC, problem set up is accomplished graphycally. For example, the configuration of a PARMILA beamline is defined by selecting icons representing transport elements from: a palette and dragging them to a window. Progress on this new approach to using PARMILA is described and example from the interface are illustrated.

articleTitle: Chordal line-integrals and the 2-D snowplow model of the microsecond plasma opening switch
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In recent years, it has become clear that MHD processes dominate the conduction phase of microsecond plasma opening switches such as HA WK and ACE-4. A useful tool for analyzing this phase is the 2-D snowplow model. The model provides an efficient way to predict the thinning of density line-integrals observed in experiments.

articleTitle: Opening switch research and development for DECADE
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: DECADE is a very high peak power generator designed to drive both large area bremsstrahlung diode arrays and imploding plasma loads. The realization of this facility required significant improvement in the operation of the critical component, the plasma opening switch (POS). This presentation will address these improvements which were made in operation of the switch, and also discuss trends in opening switch performance that have not been reported previously, and which may be due to the use of relatively long magnetically insulated transmission lines (MITL) upstream of the POS. The performance of a plasma opening switch (POS), as measured by the peak opening voltage developed, has been improved from ≈ 1.2 to ≈ 2.7 MV through reductions in the size of the cathode used, and details of the anode configuration in and downstream of the switch region. This modification was motivated by observation of electron damage to the anode in the POS region, and consisted of the removal of any metallic surfaces that exhibited significant damage and were not essential to the integri-ty of the switch.

articleTitle: Multipole field calculations for DARHT
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We calculate the beam-induced multipole fields in (a) an induction accelerating cell with two drive rods and (b) a diagnostic section of beam pipe with 4 port holes. For (a), the primary induced field is a quadrupole, while for (b), it is an octopole. The electromagnetic field solver BTEC was used to compute the field strengths in each case. Corrective measures are discussed.

articleTitle: Self-field generation in solenoidal focusing of light ion beams
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In the transport and focusing of light ion beams with a plasma filled solenoidal magnetic lens it is important to study the effect of the beams' self-fields resulting from inadequate current neutralization. Assuming complete charge neutralization, if the characteristic beam time τ satisfies 2π/Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> τ < 2π/Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>, where Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> (Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>) is the electron (plasma ion) cyclotron frequency, the plasma can be modeled as an electron magnetohydrodynamic (EMHD) fluid.
