articleTitle: Three-dimensional thermal distributions for bunched beams
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The Maxwell-Boltzmann (“thermal”) distribution of a bunched charged particle beam is the state toward which every other distribution will relax. For beams with lifetimes shorter than the time required for relaxation to equilibrium, it is the distribution at injection which minimizes the emittance growth due to relaxation toward equilibrium. Three-dimensional thermal distributions are found numerically for the case of linear external focusing forces acting on an axially symmetric bunched beam in a conducting pipe. Meta-equilibria are also found for beams with unequal transverse and longitudinal temperatures. Parameters such as perveance, emittance, space-charge tune depression, rms radius and rms bunch length are related to each other for each profile, and are given over a wide range of conditions from short to long bunches and from space-charge dominated to emittance dominated beams. Comparison is made with previous results of radial density profiles for unbunched beams and line-charge density profiles for bunched beams [1].

articleTitle: Characterization of a high-resolution framing-camera diagnostic for sabre ion beam measurements
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper presents characteristics of a high-resolution framing-camera system that has been developed for diagnosis of the SABRE ion beam. The measured temporal and spatial resolution are 6.5 ns and ∼ 1 mm respectively. Preliminary measurements of the SABRE ion beam taken immediately downstream of the diode are presented.

articleTitle: Energy resolved measurement of the characteristics of Br ion diode
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The characteristics of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>-magnetically insulated ion diode has been studied by new types of ion energy spectrometers. Dependence of the characteristics of the diode has been evaluated on the geometry of insulating magnetic field. Tum-on characteristics have been found to be improved when insulating magnetic flux (2πrdB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) increases with radius. Two dimensional, energy-resolved divergence angle of proton, carbon, oxygen, and negative ions have been evaluated independently. The divergence angle has been found to have weak dependence on energy or ion species, though ion trajectories strongly depend on them. Fine structure on the order of 1 mrad is observed in the measurement of energy-resolved injection angle distribution of the ion beam. This seems to be due to the non-uniformity of the anode plasma.

articleTitle: Energetic ions and electrons produced in a hollow cathode vacuum spark
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A vacuum spark having a tungsten pointed anode and a hollow cathode is feeded by a small Marx generator (11). It produces energetic beams of tungsten ions (E= 0.5 to 70 keV) and electrons beams in the first ignition phase. The electrons produce. an X-ray emission through Bremsstrahlung in the Tenon insulator and by Auger cascade in relation with particle emission. In the second phase. when the applied electric field is low and the current intensity is high, the electrons give rise to W (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">β</inf>) X-ray emission. The mechanism of this last part is ascribed to interactions either with the massive anode or a plasma surrounding the anode. In the case of dense plasma interaction. the emission is of the same type as observed in laser-plasma interaction. Spots of X-rays are also observed which may originate from pinching or interaction with drops or dust particles in the interelectrode spacing. Experimental results obtained using X-ray imaging are discussed.

articleTitle: Plasma lens focusing of heavy ion beams utilizing a wall-stabilized discharge
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: At the german heavy ion accelerator facility GSI different types of plasma lenses have been developed and tested. The best results were achieved with a plasma lens utilizing a wall-stabilized discharge. This type of lens has proofen to work very efficient, stable, and reproducible. A wall-stabilized plasma lens has been extensively investigated at the GSI linear accelerator UNILAC with beam energies ranging from 5.6 to 15.4 MeV /u. Several beam tests with discharge currents of up to 25 kA have shown that the focusing is mainly limited by the beam emittance of typically 5 π mm mrad and that lens related aberrations are negligible small. The concept of this wall-stabilized plasma lens has recently been extended to discharge currents above 200 kA. A first test at the SIS heavy ion synchrotron with a beam energy of 300 MeV /u has shown the same favourable behaviour of the discharge as found in the low current regime.

articleTitle: High-impedance nanosecond megavolt-range diodes
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: On the strength of experimental findings we consider problems of creating high-impedance focused and unfocused electron beams of the megavolt power level. The use of dielectric inserts with electrodes inside is shown to permit electron beam focusing at an accelerating voltage of over 1.5 MV, at currents below 10 kA, and with pulse duration of ca 50 ns

articleTitle: Dynamics of electron beam in ion undulator
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A dynamics of relativistic high-current electron beam in ion undulator is investigated. The problem of an excitation the electron radial oscillations by eans of ion Coulomb forces is under consideration. Self-consistent fields of electron beam are taken into account by using the long-wavelength stationary approximation. Two different regimes are examined. First one is the short-pulse regime when the ion background may be treated as immobile. In the second, long-pulse, case the dynamics of ions is included in consideration. The main process preventing to the excitation the large-amplitude oscillations is found. It is the phase mixing of particle's radial oscillations caused by the nonuniform radial forces. The conditions of beams injection are found when practically nondamping vibrations of electron beam occur even in long-pulse regime. This is in the case when an equilibrium injection of the ion beam takes place.

articleTitle: Relativistic magnetrons and klystrons at long pulse durations
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Extending the pulse duration of high power, relativistic microwave sources beyond ≈100 ns is a great challenge because of pulse shortening mechanisms such as gap closure and RF breakdown. We are exploring the long pulse operation of both relativistic magnetrons and relativistic klystron amplifiers. Together they represent the major classes of HPM sources: crossed field devices and linear beam tubes. We are improving the quality of the surface conditions by a variety of techniques, operating at low (∼10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup>Torr) vacuum and reducing the electric fields in the interaction region where possible. Thus far we have produced high power magnetron pulses with durations of 400 ns and conducted a beam propagation experiment on the RKA which shows stable operation for the entire duration of the electrical pulse.

articleTitle: Surface hardening of steels by high-energy electron beams of microsecond duration
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The regularities of the surface hardening and the peculiarities of the transformations in a carbon steel (0.7 % C) quenched from melt under the action of an electron beam of electron energy 160–170 keV, pulse duration 20–200 µs. and power density 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>−10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> have been studied based on heat calculations, X-ray crystal analysis and transmission electron microscopy. It has been found that maximum hardening is achieved for a pulse duration of about 40 µs. The nonmonotonic character of this dependence is accounted for by the fact that the pulse duration strongly affects the phase composition and morphology of fast-quenched steel.

articleTitle: Comparisons between simulation and experiment on a coaxial vircator high-power microwave system
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The coaxial virtual cathode oscillator (vircator) is an attempt to improve on the efficiency of the standard planar vircator. In a coaxial vircator, the cathode is a cylinder with a cold field emission treatment on the inside surface. The anode is a concentric cylinder placed inside the cathode. Electrons are accelerated in an inward radial direction and, after passing through the anode, form an oscillating space-charge cloud inside the anode.

articleTitle: Improved field geometries for SABRE extraction ion diode operation with passive ion sources
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The SABRE Facility at Sandia National Laboratories is an integrated testbed for the study of high voltage ion beam production and transport in extraction geometry for inertial confinement fusion. Our major emphasis is on the development of active ion sources, but several techniques are under investigation to improve diode performance with passive hydrocarbon and LiF ion sources. The operation of passive sources is particularly sensitive to details of the magnetic and electric field geometries and can provide insight into divergence and parasitic load mechanisms which also affect high voltage diode performance with active sources. We demonstrate that an outer cathode tip extension can eliminate cathode feed electron participation in source turn-on and virtual cathode evolution. Experimental data and TWOQUICK PIC code simulations indicate that instability-induced cross-:field diffusion of cathode tip electrons at small radius plays a dominant role in diode operation with a passive source. An improved diode geometry is presented with reduced feed electrode participation and better electron confinement at the anode emission area for lithium sources.

articleTitle: Light-Ion-beam transport research at NRL
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Ion-driven inertial confinement fusion requires transport of intense beams over several meters to isolate the ion source from the target explosion and allow for focusing and time-of-flight bunching. Transport in a low pressure background gas is possible only if rapid beam-induced gas ionization leads to formation of a plasma with electrical conductivity sufficient to charge- and current-neutralize the beam. In order to minimize collisional energy loss and scattering of the beam, helium at 1-Torr pressure is proposed for the background gas. Transport in the 1-Torr regime is not well understood because this pressure falls between the high-density regime treated by resistive models, and the low-density regime treated by collisionless models. Experiments and theoretical analyses are being carried out to study beam-induced gas ionization in this pressure regime in order to evaluate its impact on the various transport schemes including ballistic transport with solenoidal lens focusing, self-pinched transport, z-discharge transport, and wire-guided transport. Work in this area is reviewed along with other transport considerations including beam transport efficiency, beam-driven instabilities, and beam energy losses.

articleTitle: REB energy transfer in modified REBEX experiment
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The energy transfer of the relativistic electron beam (350 kV, 30 kA, 75 ns) into the intermediate dense plasma (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> <5.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−21</sup>m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>) has been studied in propagating and reflecting beam regimes at relatively short REBEX device. The performed 2µ dimensional calculation enables to estimate the conditions of the minil1111m velocity spread of the injected beam. In the case of beam injection with reduced velocity spread the saddle-like form of the plasma diamagnetism z-profile and simultaneous considerable increase of energy transfer rate has been observed, if the most beam electrons are reflected back into the plasma by virtual cathode created at the one end of the plasma column.

articleTitle: Conduction phase to opening phase transition in the plasma opening switch
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The transition between the conduction phase and opening phase of a long-conduction-time plasma opening switch (POS) is examined with the aid of numerical simulations. Evidence of three physical mechanisms is observed: magnetic pressure, magnetic field transport, and gap erosion resulting from ion acceleration out of electrostatic potential hills. Gap erosion occurs in the radial middle of the POS where the quantity B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/n is at its largest.

articleTitle: High power plasma opening switch operation on Hawk
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The Hawk pulsed power generator is used in plasma opening switch (POS) experiments in the 1-µs conduction time regime to study long conduction time switch physics. Cathode and anode geometries, especially in the switch region, can have a major impact on switch performance. There is a tradeoff between higher voltage and lower conducted current as the radius of the cathode center conductor is decreased Tapering the cathode over the switch length has produced the best performance to date: 0.7 TW at 0.75 µs conduction times with flashboard plasma sources and 1.6 MV has been generated at 1 µs conduction times with cable gun sources. There is a limit on the minimum radial gap in the switch and downstream region below which voltage and current transfer are reduced Switch performance deteriorates as the anode outer conductor just downstream of the switch, but at the same radius as the switch rods, is extended toward the load. As observed in past experiments, POS performance is independent of the plasma source used (flash boards, cable guns, or gas guns) in a given switch/load configuration. A helical center conductor in the switch region, which increases the total insulating magnetic field by a factor of 2.3, resulted in dramatically degraded switch opening for conduction times greater than 0.35 µs.

articleTitle: Generation of high-power microwave pulses of ultrashort duration
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experimental studies have been performed of the virtode, a transit-type high-power microwave pulse oscillator with a supercritical current of a relativistic electron beam (REB), and controllable frequency and output amplitude. As a result of mode selection of charge density oscillations in the electron beam, the virtode output frequency has appeared to be 4 to 5.5 GHz. Changing the phase of the UHF feedback voltage (within ±π) results in a 8 dB variation of the radiated microwave power. The highest electron efficiency of the virtode reached 17% for a pulsed microwave power of ∼ 600 MW. The dominant role of the beam mode selection in the drift region of the REB for the phase and frequency control has been demonstrated for a vircator-based combined electrodynamic system. The frequency tuning range may exceed one octave in systems incorporating a BWO. The absence of resonant elements in the virtode driving circuit makes it possible to use them for developing phase-locked high-power arrays.

articleTitle: New developments in the relativistic klystron amplifier technology
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Development of relativistic klystron amplifiers (RKAs) at NRL has set world records in peak RF power generation. Using RKAs, microwave power has been generated in excess of 10 GW at a frequency of 1.3 GHz and with energy of 1 kJ per pulse. A new generation of RKAs is being developed overcoming current limitations and providing a technology which will be compact, cheap, and equally efficient from 5 to 10 GHz (>75%). This can be achieved by using a “triaxial” RKA geometry in which an annular electron beam is surrounded on the outside and on the inside by metallic structures. This geometry can handle a large diameter electron beam of high current and high power, which is constant throughout the frequency range. Inductively loaded wide gaps, stacked with thin metallic washers, will be used to modulate the electron beam and to extract RF with high efficiency (>75%), while avoiding breakdown and DC space charge limits.

articleTitle: Studies of electron beam interaction with gas
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The res lilts of the theoretical and experimental researches of the interaction of high-intensity REBs with high density molecular gases, accomplished during last ten years in MRTI's Departmel1l of Radiation Physic and Plasma-Beam Systems, are presented. The plasma-chemical models “PC-1” and “PC-2”, gas dynamics models and beam dynamics models (WALRUS and REBUS codes) are outlined. The new equilibrium configurations of REBs with current close to the Alfven limit are found. The stable and unstable configurations are found among the equilibrium considered, and the stability region is determined. The interaction of the 3 MeV, 10 kA REB with laser formed channel 1m long in air was studied as a function (if the time delay between the channel initiation and beam injection times.

articleTitle: Negative Ions from magnetically insulated diodes
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In previous work<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> using a 1 MV, 50 ns, 7 Ω pulse line we have measured −35 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup> current density from a cylindrical diode with a polyethylene-titanium hydride cathode. Recently we have modified the system to permit radial diagnostics and the extraction of beams through four access ports. A 125 kV, 1 µs external bipolar prepulse can be used prior to the main pulse. The insulation field can be up to ∼3 Tesla and the diagnostics include Faraday cups and CR-39 track recording plastic. Cathodes constructed of different density polyethylene and polyethylene-titanium hydride composites are under study. With the new configuration we have observed 100 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup> using the polyethylene-titanium hydride cathode. In an effort to generate longer pulse duration ion beams the diode is now driven by a 650 kV, 1µs, Marx generator. We have designed and done preliminary tests on a beam forming diode which uses fiber emitters to assist surface flashover and stabilize impedance.

articleTitle: Physics of electron emission from metal-dielectric cathodes
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The present paper gives a description of the metal-dielectric cathode operation. There is an explosive electron emission on the cathodes, that occurs through explosions of the metal micro protrusions at so-called triple points (metal-dielectric-vacuum). The current of a vacuum discharge over dielectric surface plays its initiating part. Such a mechanism of emission is operating in low-voltage ferroelectric cathodes, in cathodes of long service in high-power pulse repetitive accelerators as well as in the cathodes used in focusing high power electron beams.

articleTitle: Resonant and chaotic phenomena in a periodically focused intense charged-particle beam
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The exploration of the characteristics of periodically focused intense charged particle beams is one of the main thrusts in beam physics research and is critical to many advanced accelerator applications such as heavy ion fusion. In this paper, we discuss several novel effects induced by the self-electric and self-magnetic fields of an intense beam in a periodic focusing channel consisting of either a periodic solenoidal field or an alternating-gradient quadrupole magnetic field. It is shown that the self fields induce rich nonlinear resonances and chaotic behavior in the envelope oscillations of mismatched beams. A parametric instability threshold is derived analytically for halo formation in a mismatched space-charge-dominated beam and is found to be in good agreement with two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations. For envelope-matched beams with nonuniform density profiles, single-particle orbits are also found to exhibit nonlinear resonances and chaotic behavior in high-current regimes, suggesting a microscopic mechanism for emittance growth. The implications of these findings are discussed regarding the design of high-current accelerators and high-current transport systems.

articleTitle: Computational modeling of magnetized target fusion experiments
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The advent of 100-MJ-class flux compression generators<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,2</sup> has made it possible to consider driving fusion targets by direct magnetic implosion<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, with implosion kinetic energies far beyond those available with conventional fusion drivers. Computational studies have suggested that the optimal use of such energy is in a magnetized target fusion (MTF) system<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>

articleTitle: Magnetic field distribution and shell structure in a gas-puff Z-pinch plasma
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The plasma properties during the implosion phase in a gas-puffed Z-pinch are studied from time-dependent spectral shapes and intensities of emission lines of singly to five times ionized ions measured in various directions. The magnetic field distribution in the plasma is determined from Zeeman splitting by discrimination against the Stark and Doppler broadenings using polarization spectroscopy. The skin depth obtained implies a classical plasma conductivity. The dependence of the radial charge-state distribution on the axial dimension is studied in detail. The ion velocities are found to vary along the axis, however the radial charge-state distribution and the radially propagating ionization wave previously observed are seen to occur similarly in all axial locations.

articleTitle: Circuit characterization of magnetically insulated electron flow
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We consider a switch characteristic corresponding to magnetically insulated electron flow in a gap between an effective cathode and anode. The current voltage relationship in a circuit containing parallel switch and load elements remains that of the switch independent of the load for load impedance which is not too small. This concept to which the analytic model investigated in this paper conforms is confirmed by two-dimensional PIC calculations for electron flow in a magnetically insulted gap leading into a vacuum feed terminated by a resistive load.

articleTitle: Experimental research of electron magneto-hydrodynamics effects in microsecond POS
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The paper presents new data aimed at understanding and characterizing of microsecond Plasma Opening Switch (POS) plasma. In planar geometry both optical and probe experiments were carried out in two regimes. Erosion regime with sharp current interruption is characterized by current penetration with a velocity 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> cm/s through plasma having its impedance at several Ohms from current beginning. Ion probes show substantial ion current along all POS cathode area. In another regime with higher plasma concentration there is no sharp switching, plasma has high conductivity and current penetrates into plasma an order as slow. Electron-image frames show instabilities at the last stage of rising current that could be important illustration when considering Electron magneto HydroDynamic (EHD) effects.

articleTitle: Gyrotwistrons as a source for future particle accelerators
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The use of gyrotwistrons as a source for particle acceleration is discussed. Experimental results for a device utilizing a 440 kV, 200–245 A, 1 µs electron beam and a sharply tapered axial magnetic field are presented. Both fundamental and second harmonic operation are reported. Mode competition and its possible remedies are considered.

articleTitle: Beam-plasma discharge in the ionosphere during active experiments
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A model of the beam-plasma discharge with regards to active experiments with injections of powerful electron beams in the ionosphere was developed. Main features of the beam-plasma interaction are spacecraft charging, the plasma turbulence generation, fast increase of the ambient plasma density, heating and acceleration of the background electrons. These processes collectively determine the propagation of the injected electron beam into the ambient ionospheric plasma. It is well known that there are some peculiarities of beam-plasma interaction was observed during electron beam injection into ionospheric plasma. Among them are luminosity of the near rocket region, intensive high-frequency electromagnetic radiation, anomalous scattering of the beam electrons near a rocket, intensive optical and infrared radiation from the discharge region. Two-dimensional electromagnetic particle simulations have been carried out in order to investigate the injection and transport of the dense electron beam from the spacecraft into ionospheric plasma. The obtained main characteristics of the beam-ionospheric plasma interaction permit to explain some pecularities of the active experiments.

articleTitle: Ectons in high power charged particle accelerators
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: It has been shown that there are many ways of energy concentration in cathode microvolumes of up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> Jig, which lead to microexplosions accompanied by electron emission. The process lasts not longer than 9–10 seconds and then ceases. If the current exceeds a threshold value, the process becomes self-sustaining. The phenomenon is named “ecton”. The threshold current value corresponds to a certain critical mass of the material exploded. Assuming that the Joule radius is equal to the radius of thermal conductivity, the paper presents a simple model of the ecton.

articleTitle: “Catalytic resonance ionization” - A novel universal technique for the formation of a two-component anode-plasma
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this paper we describe a technique to produce planar and volumetric ion sources of nearly every element. This technique is based on a generalization of the LIBORS-process (Laser Ionization Based On Resonant Saturation) which because of its similarity to chemical catalytic reactions has been called CATRION (CAT-alytic Resonance IONization). A vapor containing the desired atomic species is doped with a suitable element possessing resonance transitions that can be pumped to saturation with a laser. By superelastic collisions with the excited atoms and by stimulated bremsstrahlung absorption seed electrons are heated and multiplied. It is the heated electron component which then by collisional processes also ionizes the desired atomic species. This technique will work efficient if both the atom and the ion of the dopant posses resonant transitions that can be pumped by the same laser. Instead of using tunable dye lasers we propose to apply gas lasers which are more robust and appropriate for repetitive long term operation. We present a large number of coincidences between gas laser wavelength and resonant transitions in suitable atoms.

articleTitle: Investigation of beam acceleration and extraction on a stellatron
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The stellatron accelerator of the University of California at Irvine (UCI) [Phys. Fluids B2, 3149 (1990)] was modified to accommodate beam extraction. The magnetic field coils were reconstructed to adapt an extraction port. A fiberglass-graphite-epoxy chamber replaced the glass chamber that cracked frequently during the previous experiment. Improvement in the magnetic field configuration has significantly reduced the current loss during acceleration. A 1.1 kA, 12 MeV electron beam was generated by initially forming a 1.2 kA beam with plasma start-up. The beam radius was 5–7 mm. Beam extraction was performed with two auxiliary pulsed current coils and up to 15% of the beam was extracted from the chamber. The extraction process was analyzed by computational orbit simulations.

articleTitle: High current beam propagation studies at the naval research laboratory
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experiments have been performed on the production, conditioning, and propagation of high current electron beams using NRL's SuperIBEX generator.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> The objective of these experiments has been to produce high current density electron beams that are able to propagate multiple betatron wavelengths without suffering disruptive hose growth. The key to producing a hose-stable high current beam is to condition the beam by damping radial perturbations and tailoring the emittance profile to prevent growth of the instability. Results from recent experiments on beam production, conditioning, and propagation will be presented.

articleTitle: Fast ion heating due to REB-induced plasma turbulence
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experimental investigation of the relativistic electron beam (REB) energy transfer to the ion plasma component in the REBEX machine is reported The presented estimates of the ion temperature are based on the intracavity laser spectroscopic measurements of the H a line profiles and on the time-of-flight analysis of fast charge-exchange neutrals. The results of optical diagnostics indicate that ions gain energy during the 100 ns REB injection, e.g. much faster than it would correspond to the collisional energy transfer from the REB-heated plasma electrons. The mean energy of the plasma ion component at the end of the beam injection is comparable or even higher than the electron temperature of the bulk. A turbulent mechanism which might be responsible for the observed fast ion heating is discussed

articleTitle: Gas-puff z-pinch driven by inductive pulsed power generator
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Inductive energy storage pulsed power generator ASO-II was used as a power source of gas-puff z-pinch. A uniform discharge was obtained, and a z-pinch implosion occurred at higher driving current than that of fast bank. The intensity of soft x-ray radiated from the plasma was larger than that from the plasma driven by the fast bank. From the observation of hot spots by a pin-hole camera, the spatial positions of hot spots did not much move shot to shot. These results are very important for industorial applications of the gas-puff z-pinch.

articleTitle: First experimental observation of switching the microsecond electron beam by reconnection of the magnetic field lines
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The paper presents the experimental results on fast (∼10µs) switching of the microsecond ribbon (1×12cm) REB by reconnection of the guiding magnetic field lines. Conditions for switching the electron beam from one channel to another has been found. High efficiency of the beam transport through the switching unit has been obtained.

articleTitle: Research on S-band injector of 1+1/2 cavity with thermionic cathode
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An S-band injector of 1+1/2 microwave cavity. with thermionic cathode and operating at frequency of 2998 MHz. has being theoretically and experimentally researched at the Institute of Applied Electronics. CAEP. The injector consists of 1+1/2 accelerating cavities with side coupler and the cavity design is optimized by ourselves. The emitting material of cathode is single-crystal lanthanum hexaboride (LaB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>). It is expermentally observed that macropulse current is 1.67 A and its electron energy 0.8 MeV under the repeat frequency of 50 Hz.

articleTitle: Anomalous braking of scanning REB and high-power EMP excitation near a conductive surface
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of numerical simulation of high-power EMP excitation by scanning REB suggested in [1] and its anomalous braking near a conductive surface (metallic coaxial) are presented. The results occur more optimistical than it was supposed in [1]. Namely, the energetical pumping of EMP is continued at the nonlinear stage even when the reflected beam electrons appear and beam braking takes place. The EMP broading at this stage remains negligible and becomes significant only after the REB being switched off.

articleTitle: High power light ion beams at aea technology, Culham
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: High power particle beams have been under development at AEA Technology, Culham for over 20 years. Initially directed towards the requirements of the fusion programmes at JET and Culham, the applications now include defence and industrial fields. The work described here concentrates on the production of negative ions for fusion and defence.

articleTitle: High current beam emissions from spacecraft
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: During high current charged particle beam emissions from a spacecraft, the spacecraft potential floats relative to the ambient plasma. There are important questions about the upper limits of beam current emitted into the ambient plasma and of the spacecraft potential. The usually accepted view is that the beam current emitted reaches its upper limit when the spacecraft potential reaches the beam energy. In this view, any attempt to emit a current beyond the critical value would result in partial beam return while both the effective beam current emitted and the spacecraft potential would remain unaffected. Surprisingly, results from three recent beam experiments in space show that the spacecraft potential can exceed the beam energy when very high beam currents are emitted. These results show that the usual limits on the beam current emitted and the spacecraft potential achieved are incorrect. Study of space charge beam divergence shows that the usual limits can be exceeded.

articleTitle: Intense electron-beam transport in the ion-focused regime through the collision-dominated regime
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper reviews the transport of the 19-MeV, 700-kA, 25-ns Hermes-III electron beam in long gas cells filled with N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas spanning six decades in pressure from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> to ∼10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> Torr. We show through measurements and theoretical analyses that the beam has two windows of. stable transport: a low-pressure window (between ∼1 and ∼100 Torr) that is dominated by propagation in the semi-collisionless IFR (ion-focused regime), and a high-pressure window (between ∼1 and ∼100 Torr) that is dominated by propagation in the resistive CDR (collision-dominated regime). In the CDR, 79±1.5% of the beam energy is transported over 11 m at 20 Torr. In the IFR we show that intense radiation fields with controllable rise times and pulse widths can be generated on axis at a bremsstrahlung target. In summary, the measurements and analyses presented here provide a quantitative description of the Hermes-III beam transport over six decades in pressure.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional numerical simulation of imploding plasma liners
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A computation analysis is performed to investigate 2D effects in imploding plasma liners. Some mechanisms degrade radiation output in the systems: the development of Rayleigh-Taylor (RT) type instabilities, “zippering” effect and instability of magnetized electrons current sheet. For the compressed double gas-puffs external axial magnetic field stabilizes short wavelength R-T instability. All these effects are studied numerically. The calculations were carried out using 2D three-temperature code TIGR-M. To predict liner shapes from supersonic gas puff injection, driven by time-dependent power pulse some calculations have been made. Dynamics of plasma in three-temperature MHD with Hall term is discussed.

articleTitle: A new configuration of vircator for efficient, narrow-bandwidth microwave generation
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A new configuration of virtual cathode oscillator (vircator) was investigated by numerical calculation using particle-in-cell simulation code. In this configuration, a cylindrical cavity is located between the electron beam source and the waveguide. Simulation results show that the vircator oscillation in the waveguide is determined by the cavity mode. As a result, the microwave amplitude is not affected by the electron energy spread of 3 %, and no significant change of the oscillation frequency is observed even with a 25 % variation of the electron current.

articleTitle: Driver coupling to quasi static z-pinches
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Quasistatic Z-pinches formed “on axis” and magnetically confined by a current larger than a critical current (> 1.5 MA for deuterium) undergo radiative collapse providing high density thermal plasmas. Z-pinches created from solid fibers do not well couple to the driver due to lacking initial conductivity and compressibility resulting in fast plasma expansion and current leaks. Especially fiber experiments performed with high power drivers (necessary to rapidly force radiative collapse) tend to escape close coupling. Therefore experiments starting from plasmajets (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sup> − 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> = 0.5 − 1 eV) have been carried out at the pulseline KALIF (2 MV, 900 kA) and at the fast condensor bank SPEED 1 (200 kv: 900 kA). All plasmajet experiments show a better initial coupling than fiber experiments. Unfortunately, the KALIF driver is decoupled from the load by rapid plasma erosion taking place typically 50 ns after ignition. This is due to high values of the reduced electric field (E/n > 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−15</sup> Vm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) causing runaway electrons and preventing sheath formation. Since this decoupling was avoided in SPEED 1 experiments (E/n < 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−17</sup> Vm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) high power experiments need plasmajets with densities in the order of n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">24</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>.

articleTitle: High power electron generators based on charging of a pulse-forming line by means of electrically exploded wires
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Most of the currently operating high-power megampere generators have been developed in one of two circuit designs. In the former case, the generator consists of a high-operating-voltage (HV) microsecond Marx generator (U > 1.5 – 2 MV), several cascades of water pulse-forming lines (FL) , a transmission line, and a vacuum diode. In the latter case, these are a rather low-operating-voltage (LV) microsecond Marx (U < 1 MV), an inductive energy store, a POS, and a proper diode. Each of these circuit designs has certain deficiencies. In the former case, these are the well-known operating difficulties with the HV Marx (more stringent requirements the insulation and the bulky element base), and the presence of bulky microsecond FLs with their provision systems, that increase the installation size. In the latter case, these are a rather low switch resistance at the stage of current switching into a load, hence, a slightly increased output voltage and, particularly, power. At the same time, there exist well-known low-current high-power HV e-beam generators, which are built in the circuit design including a LV (∼ 1 MV) microsecond Marx, an inductive energy store, an exploding wire (EW) switch, and a vacuum diode. In such generators, the above mentioned problems are solved by increasing the initial voltage four to six times. But these circuits have a low energy efficiency (< 30 %) related to the EW operation into a resistive load (diode). However, it can be supposed that a capacitive load, because of its specific impedance, may have a higher energy efficiency for the same maximum voltages. Thereby, we consider the operation of the high-power high-current generator (HPHCG) with the circuit design “LV Marx - inductive storage - EW switch - fast FL - transmission line - diode”. Here the main problem is the efficiency of energy transfer from the Marx to the HV-FL. Some relevant information is in Refs. 1 and 2.

articleTitle: Control of a large vacuum wave precursor on the sabre voltage adder MITL and extraction ion diode
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: SABRE is a ten-cavity magnetically insulated voltage adder (6 MV, 300 kA) used to study ion beam production in high voltage extraction applied-B ion diodes. Observations indicate that the machine power initially propagates in a large-amplitude vacuum wave prior to electron emission. This vacuum wave “precursor” has an important impact on the turn-on and impedance history of ion diodes. Typical precursor characteristics are shown using transmission line, diode, and beam current and voltage data and are compared to TWOQUICK PIC-code simulations. Two techniques are under investigation to control the precursor and its effects on diode performance. A plasma opening switch (POS) has been used to erode the precursor. Field enhancing inserts are also planned to decrease the macroscopic fields required for electron emission from the cathode. This will limit the distance over which vacuum and insulated waves separate due to propagation at different velocities. Experimental data from the POS technique and TWOQUICK simulations of the insert technique are presented and discussed

articleTitle: Applications of large-scale electromagnetic and particle-in-cell simulation models to rf devices and components
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Large-scale simulation codes have matured to the point where they can be applied to the design of high-power beam and rf devices. These codes offer the capability to carry out self-consistent computations of beam dynamics and electromagnetic fields in the presence of complicated, realistic geometrical configurations and volumetric materials. SAIC's MASK and ARGUS codes are general-purpose simulation tools in two and three dimensions, respectively. They have been used in government and commercial laboratories in the design of diverse devices, such as accelerator components, antennas, diodes, MIMIC's, and microwave tubes. Over the past three years, these codes have been incorporated into simulation-based design systems, such as SAIC's CFA Design System for crossed-field amplifiers and the MMACE (Microwave and Millimeter Wave Advanced Computational Environment) design framework for helix TWT's and other rf power tubes. In these computational frameworks, the simulation codes are linked to other design and engineering tools through standard data transfer protocols that allow data to flow seamlessly from a user interface through a hierarchy of design and modeling tools. This paper will include examples of the application of these tools in the design of crossed-field amplifiers, helix TWT's, and diamond reactors.

articleTitle: Formation of an electron beam in its squeezed state
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of the computer simulations of electron beam emission and propagation in various spatially inhomogeneous systems are presented. It is shown that with the appropriate choice of the geometrical parameters the beam may be created in its squeezed state.

articleTitle: Ferroelectric electron beam sources
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Ferroelectric materials offer the possibility of compact electron sources, with modest requirements to initiate the emission process. We are studying such sources as possible injectors for microwave generation. The source consists of a polarized ferroelectric ceramic disk with silver electrodes coated on both faces. The front electrode consists of a periodic grid created by etching the silver to expose a line pattern of ceramic. This electrode functions as the cathode in a planar diode geometry with an accelerating gap adjustable from 0.1 to 5 cm. A rapid change in the polarization state of the ceramic is achieved by applying a 1–2 kV, 150 ns pulse between the electrodes of the ferroelectric. Early work used a coaxial cable to maintain an anode potential of up to 1 kV across the A-K gap. The emitted electron current was measured as a function of the gap spacing and the anode potential. The current varies linearly with the anode voltage, up to 1 kV, for gaps < 10 mm, and typically exceeds the Child-Langmuir current density by at least two orders of magnitude. Current densities in excess of 70 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> have been measured. More recent work has used a 300 ns pulse forming network to apply a potential of up to 15 k V at the anode. Results of emittance and' scaling measurements under these conditions are reported.

articleTitle: Kα spectral diagnostics for Mg and Al plasmas irradiated by intense Li beams
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> spectroscopy can be a valuable diagnostic method for determining plasma conditions in ion beam-heated targets. In intense light ion beam experiments, K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> emission lines can be observed as 2p electrons drop down to fiU1s vacancies created by beam-impact ionization. In this paper, we present results from collisional-radiative equilibrium (CRE) calculations for Al and Mg target tracer layers being irradiated by an intense Li beam. Presently, 9 MeV Li beams with power densities of 1–2 TW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> can be generated in Particle Beam Fusion Accelerator-II (PBFA-II) experiments at Sandia National Laboratories. It is shown that both emission and absorption K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> spectra show good sensitivity to temperature and density for the range of plasma conditions typically achieved in present PBFA-II experiments.

articleTitle: Relativistic Peniotron experiment at JAERI
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A version of Peniotoron experiment using an IREB has been studied at JAERI, to see if its concept still works and the high conversion efficiency is preserved with relativistic and intense electron beam. A hollow rotating electron beam (0.9MV,400A and 100ns) was injected into a cylindrical cavity immersed in a 3kG static field to cause an interaction of the beam and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">211</inf> mode of the cavity. Several kinds of intense microwave bursts were found in the frequency rclI1ge of 2–5GHz. Some of them could be due to CARM, while the identification of peniotron radiation was less credible. Generation of the hollow rotating beam and analyses of the radiation process are presented.

articleTitle: Initial characterization of Z-pinch load discharges on the ACE 4 pulse generator
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Recently the first Z-pinch load experiments were performed on ACE 4. Interesting results were obtained on two shots operating with 5 cm diameter neon gas puffs in direct drive mode (no operation of the radial plasma opening switch (POS)). Pinhole images obtained with implosion times greater than 300 ns suggested compression ratios of at least 25. If such implosion times ultimately prove feasible for operation with a POS, requirements for POS rise time and voltage could be significantly relaxed from present projections.

articleTitle: Construction and test-operation of apparatus for interaction between pulsed ion beam and gaseous target
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Preliminary results are described about the construction and test-operation of our apparatus, which has aims to inject various kinds of intense pulsed ion beams into medium pressure targets of neutral gases or plasmas, and to measure various cross sections for charge exchange or multiple-ionization, for example. The purpose of the research is to gather the fundamental data for the ionic collision processes.

articleTitle: Simulation of flashover generated by strong tem-wave in MITL with inner coaxial dielectric insert
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Extremely sharp rise time of high-power relativistic electron beam was achieved by using of the long dielectric insert build into the cathode line of the magnetically insulated transmission line (MITL)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. Presented paper is devoted to a theoretical treatment of this process. Efficiency of the sharp front formation grows owing to its dependence on the speed of the flashover front propagation. So, an estimation of this dependence is a step of great importance in solution of the problem. To do this, the problem of TEM - wave diffraction on the coaxial line and dielectric insert conjunction has been solved rigorously. It allows the electric field to be found at any time moment and at any point of dielectric. The flashover front speed has been estimated on physical grounds which can be derived from experimental data for the early phase of dielectric surface flashover in vacuum.

articleTitle: PBF A-II modification for high-power high-convergence implosion experiments
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A linear inductive voltage adder design for PBFA II is presented that could permit high convergence radiatively-driven implosion experiments with two ring-shaped two-stage extraction diodes. The design incorporates two linear inductive voltage adder modules with ferromagnetically-loaded cavities, one for the upper half and another for the lower half of PBFA II, and can be positioned vertically or horizontally in a head-to-head linear configuration with the diodes at the center. The design provides a total of ∼ 20-MV and 100-TW electrical power delivered to the diodes. If diode, ion, and transport efficiencies are taken into account, the design is capable of depositing 55 TW to a 6-mm diameter target, which corresponds to a specific peak power density of 50 TW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Virtual cathode in magnetic self insulated transmission line, structure, and theory
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The feasibility of vircator existence in a MITL is demonstrated in this report. We describe some structural peculiarities of vircator formation in such lines and discuss the nature of electron motion in such vircator. Usually, in the line only the potential monotones radial profiles become realizable with zero electric field on the cathode. The pre-supposed vircator existence leaves a possibility of finding solutions, involving the potential trough.

articleTitle: Beam-plasma discharge during the long-pulse REB injection in rarefied gas
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Numerical simulation results of the interaction of a long-pulse relativistic electron beam (REB) with a slightly ionized middle pressure (p ∼ 1 Tor) gas in conditions of the beam-plasma discharge without external magnetic field are presented The next beam and plasma parameters were used in calculations: beam density n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, beam radius a = 0.5 cm, particles energy W = 0.3 MeV, pulse duration τ = 50 µs, front duration τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> = 1 µs, initial air plasma temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eo</inf> = 0.15 e V, initial plasma density N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eo</inf> = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, system length L = 100 cm. The dissipative beam-plasma instability develops and the beam-plasma discharge ignites already in the current pulse front. To the moment t = 5 µs the beam-plasma discharge has turned to the quasi-stationary state, characterized by the level of the HF electric fields E ∼ 1 kV/cm. almost homogeneous distribution of the temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> ≈ 2 eV and inhomogeneous distribution of the plasma density n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>. In time the gas heating takes place, mainly owing to the heat produced by the dissociative recombination of the plasma electrons and ions. Gas temperature T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> increases from the room value to T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> ≥ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> K.

articleTitle: A large-area X-ray diode for the SNOP accelerator
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An investigation of the possibility to form nanosecond electron beams has been performed on the SNOP-I and SNOP-2 generators with the goal to create X-ray sources for testing objects of area 5 to 3000 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The experiments were carried out at voltages 0.4 to 1 MV, currents 200 to 600 A, and beam energies 10 to 20 kJ. Diodes with pinching, annular, and sheet beams were tested. It has been demonstrated that the decelerators can be smoothly tuned for irradiation of objects of area 5 to 3000 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a rather good energy matching between the accelerator and the diode.

articleTitle: Investigation of plasma producing by an electron beam in a gas filled set of coupled cavities
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The model of plasma producing in a gas by an electron beam is considered for the case of its propagation in a thin long tube in the presence of an axial magnetic field. Plasma is produced by means of ionization of neutral molecules by electrons of a beam and plasma. Plasma particles losses are conditioned with leaving of electrons for the tube ends and leaving of ions in the transverse direction for its lateral walls. The formula for plasma density obtained using the balance of its particles describes qualitatively rightly the process of plasma producing by an electron beam. Estimations demonstrate the satisfactory accordance with an experiment.

articleTitle: Plasma liner implosion with microturbulence effects consideration
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The focus of the paper is on the coupling between double gas-puff dynamics and anomalous effects associated with microinstabilities development. Two anomalous collisional models have been considered: ion-acoustic model and model for lower-hybrid-drift instability. All calculations have been carried out using 1D radiation Lagrangian MHD code ERA. It is found that numerical results taking into account anomalous collisions are more closed to the experimental data.

articleTitle: Experiments with microsecond Magnetically Controlled Plasma Opening Switch
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Presented are the results obtained in recent Magnetically Controlled Plasma Opening Switch experiments in submicrosecond conduction time range on the terawatt GIT-4 pulser at Institute of High Current Electronics. The opening time control was provided by variation of both slow magnetic field and fast magnetic field amplitudes in switch region. The additional trigger Plasma Opening Switch placed in fast coil circuit allowed to vary the fast coil “turn-on” and risetime of fast magnetic field. We investigated switch performance for both plasma injection directions: along slow magnetic field lines and across them. The coaxial inductance or electron beam diode served for a load in the experiments. The switching characteristics were studied as functions of plasma parameters.

articleTitle: Using a radially divergent e-beam accelerator to irradiate flue gases
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A wide-aperture radially divergent e-beam accelerator is described in the paper. Also results of experiments on the use of the accelerator for removal of sulphur oxides from a gas mixture, modelling a flue gas composition, are presented. The electron accelerator uses a low-pressure-arc-discharge-formed plasma cathode. The Marx generator is applied for power supply of the accelerator. Radially divergent e-beam with an electron energy of 300 ke V, generated in the accelerating gap, is led out into the atmosphere through a 1.5 m - area thin foil. The irradiated gas volume is about 170 I. A possibility of SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> oxidation chain plasma-chemical reaction realization is shown in the experiments on model mixtures with SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> content up to 1%. Minimum energy losses to remove one SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> molecule amounting to less than 1 e V /mol are achieved with an optimal e-beam current density of ∼ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It is shown that energy losses are determined not only e-beam current density but also by the duration of its pulse.

articleTitle: MRTI activity in the field of accelerators 1946–1992
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: From 1946 through 1992 the Moscow Radiotechnical Institute of Russian Academy of Sciences (MRT I) participated in the development of accelerators: Phasotron, various Proton Synchrotrons, Accelerating and Storage Complex (UNK), Linear Proton Accelerators, Meson Physics Facility Accelerator, Linear Electron Accelerators and the Industrial High Voltage Accelerator. The parameters of these accelerators are described in the paper.

articleTitle: The transition from the magnetic focusing of the relativistic electron beam to the ion-focused regime
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The REB dynamic in the region of the transition from magnetic focusing to the ion one has been examined, The azimuth-symmetric system has been considered. The field calculations have been performed under, long-wave approximation. For beam description the Vlasov equation has been treated by the particle method The emittance and the current of the beam after the transition region have been determined as a function of the ion channel radius; the channel density, the electron energy. the transfer region length. The transition from the focusing by the longitudinal magnetic field to the ion focused regime has been shown to be worthwhile when beam electron energies are so that the self beam field influence is negligible. The beam parameters after consistence period has weak dependence on the transition region length (if it is larger than two betatron lengths) and on the character of the magnetic field reduction. A t the consistence region the ion channel radius must be larger than the beam radius at least during the initial time intervals.

articleTitle: Numerical study of relativistic electron beam pumping by virtual cathode
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this article a new method for electron beam pumping by means of virtual cathode is proposed. The electron beam is generated in a foilless diode, whose anode tube is connected directly to a wider output drift tube. The emitted by cold plasma emission from hollow cathode electrons propagate in an external homogeneous magnetic field. The virtual cathode is formed at the wide drift tube entrance. Computer simulations show an essential beam pumping behind the virtual cathode. The transmitted electron beam pitch-ratio ex reaches value above 1 which is sufficient for development of the maser instability.

articleTitle: Use of pulsed e-beams for the initiation of spectral luminescence in solids
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The work is devoted to the pulsed cathodoluminescence (PCL) of solids that occurs upon irradiating them latter by high-current pulsed e-beams. The parameters of e-beams that cause no irreversible disintegration in the material under investigation are given. The conclusion has been made that PCL can be used in a spectral-emission analysis of solids being single-piece structures, thereby offering a new field of application for electron beams.

articleTitle: Experimental study of the high power broadband microwave emission from beam-plasma interaction
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We have carried out experiments on interaction of an intense relativistic electron beam (IREB) with a plasma which is an interesting subject from a point of view of nonlinear phenomena. From the interaction broadband microwaves radiated and its power reached about 2 MW. For the radiation, the ratio of the beam and the plasma densities (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>/n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>) is an important parameter. We found that there was an optimum on n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>/n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> at which the power density in the observing window (18 – 40 GHz) was maximum. When the value of n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>/n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> was among 0.001∼0.01, the radiated microwave was intensified. An existence of the optimum condition can be explained by an energy input from beam to plasma by two stream instability.

articleTitle: Ion Beam Surface Treatment: A new capability for surface enhancement
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The emerging capability to produce high average power (5–350 kW) pulsed ion beams at 0.2–2 MeV energies is enabling us to develop a new, commercial-scale thermal surface treatment technology called Ion Beam Surface Treatment (IBEST). This new technique uses high energy, pulsed (5.250 ns) ion beams to directly deposit energy in the top 2–20 micrometers of the surface of any material. The depth of treatment is controllable by varying the ion energy and species. Deposition of the energy with short pulses in a thin surface layer allows melting of the layer with relatively small energies and allows rapid cooling of the melted layer by thermal diffusion into the underlying substrate. Typical cooling rates of this process (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> K/sec) cause rapid resolidification, resulting in the production of non-equilibrium microstructures (nano-crystalline and metastable phases) that have significantly improved corrosion, wear, and hardness properties. We have conducted IBEST feasibility experiments with results confirming surface hardening, nanocrystaline grain formation, metal surface polishing, controlled melt of ceramic surfaces, and surface cleaning using puilsed ion beams.

articleTitle: Cyclotron-Cherenkov instability in dielectric-loaded circular waveguides
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: When a linear electron beam is injected into a dielectric-loaded waveguide immersed in an axial magnetic field, Cherenkov and cyclotron-Cherenkov instabilities appear. We report computational results on linear growth rates of both instabilities for three types of waveguides. For the first type which consists of a metallic cylinder with dielectric liner on the inner surface, the growth rate of Cherenkov instability is larger than that of cyclotron-Cherenkov instability. For the second type which consists of a dielectric core and an outer metallic cylinder, both growth rates are comparable. For the third type which consists of a metallic core with dielectric liner on the surface and an outer metallic cylinder, the growth rates of the latter instability is higher than that of the former. The case of the third type is investigated at some length. Effects of thermal spread of the beam are included.

articleTitle: 2D simulations of cascade magneto cumulative generators in euler-lagrange variables
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The A.I.Pavlovskii's cascade magnetocumulative generator (MC-1) has been studied with the aid of the TIGR-M implicit simulational technique which is designed for computation of 2D MHD flows of heat-conducting gas in complex systems. The TIGR-M computations of 2D axially asymmetric perturbations development in i-cascade MC generator show that in the process of magnetocumulative motion the curvature of the inside liner boundary reverses (even twice) in the points of internal shell boundary: concavity becomes convexity and alternatively.

articleTitle: Flexural waves induced by a high current electron beam in a thin plate
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Intense flexural waves excited in thin plates by a nanosecond pulsed power electron beam are investigated by the laser interferometry method and theoretically. Experiments were made for thin round plates made of fused silica, aluminum alloy, and composite of carbon fibers in epoxy matrix. The calculation method is developed in terms of the thermoelasticity linear theory. The numerical results appear to be in a good agreement with the experimental data. Especially good agreement is observed for the brittle material (fused silica) due to its better elasticity. The analysis of theoretical and experimental results shows that the excitation of flexural waves as well as longitudinal waves is the primary effect of exciting a solid by pulsed electron beam. Clarity of the experimental situation and sufficient agreement with the theory allow us to determine some important constants of a material, such as Poisson's ratio, Young's modulus, Grüneisen's parameter.

articleTitle: First operation of new inductive accelerating module at JAERI
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A new electron induction acceleration unit is completed and operated at JAERI. Several new technologies are involved therein: (1)New Fe-based nanocryostal-line soft magnetic material “Finemet” is used in foil. Its higher saturation flux density and lower power loss than the other Fe based amorphous alloys improves the performance. (2) The waveform of the accelerating voltage can be kept constant within ±1 % during the pulse, and moreover the ramp of the pulse can be varied in the range of +/− 200 kV/130ns. (3) The accelerating units are divided into two parts: One is for the beam generation and the other for the post acceleration. The latter is fabricated so that the driving circuit be separated from the acceleration column. A final beam of 2.5 MeV (variable for 1.3−2.5 MeV), 3 kA and 160 ns flat top is expected. The results of a cold test of the system combined with the power supply and acceleration cell are given.

articleTitle: Experimental studies of electron beam explosive high-power generators
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Analysis data, presented in a paper, shows that electron beam generators, powered by magnetic cumulative generators are better then those described in pUblications by compactness, transportability and specific energy characteristics.

articleTitle: Ion-hose instability of the relativistic electron beam in rarefied gas
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The ionization processes influence on the ion hose instability in the relativistic electron beams propagating through a rarefied gas in the ion1ocused regime is investigated theoretically. The contributions of the collision ionization of the gas in the channel by the beam electrons and channel ions are taken into account, as well as one of the resonant ions charge exchange. The task is solved using the nonlinear kinetic model under the paraxial quasistatic approach for planar geometry of the beam and the channel It is shown that as the gas pressure in the channel rises the instability linear stage characterized by the highest increment prolongs, leading to a higher saturation level of the electron beam mass center oscillations with respect to one at a lower pressure. The prolongation of the resonant linear stage of the instability is assumed to occur due to that reason, that in the considered case of the moderate oscillation amplitudes the new ions production happens mainly as result of the collision ionization by the electrons assisting to the accordance of the beam and the channel distortions.

articleTitle: Time resolved multi-dimensional diagnostics for intense ion beams
publicationTitle: 1994 10th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An Arrayed Pinhole Camera (APC) can measure spatial distributions of beam divergence and flux, simultaneously. A time resolved two-dimensional (radial and azimuthal) APC has developed. Achieved performance of the APC are a spatial resolution on anode of better than 1 mm, and an effective divergence resolution of better than 10 mrad. The measured beams are an energy of about 0.5 MeV, an ion current density of about 10 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> proton and carbon beam, which was generated by a beam-extraction type applied-B two-stage diode. The insulation magnetic field of the diode was varied for improve beam distributions. Time evolutions of divergence distributions are acquired.
